content: The Oregon College of Oriental Medicine (OCOM) is situated in Portland, Oregon, in the United States. It provides both master's and postgraduate doctoral degree programs specializing in acupuncture and Oriental medicine. The institution's academic programs are fully accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Acupuncture and Oriental Medicine. Additionally, it is authorized by the Oregon Student Assistance Commission's Office of Degree Authorization to confer degrees such as the Master of Acupuncture and Oriental Medicine (MAcOM) and the Doctor of Acupuncture and Oriental Medicine (DAOM). OCOM operates an Intern Teaching Clinic and an herbal dispensary, which serve the Portland metropolitan area. This clinic provides over 20,000 patient treatments annually at a reduced cost. These treatments include acupuncture, Chinese herbal medicine, tuina (a form of Chinese therapeutic massage), and shiatsu (a Japanese bodywork therapy). The clinic also functions as a hands-on teaching facility for OCOM students, allowing them to gain practical experience under supervision. In July 2005, OCOM achieved a significant milestone by becoming the first institution to graduate a cohort of students with Doctor of Acupuncture and Oriental Medicine (DAOM) degrees. The college also maintains an active research department, which has been awarded substantial funding from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and the National Center for Complementary and Alternative Medicine (NCCAM). One of its current research initiatives includes a collaborative project with the University of Arizona, focusing on the study of temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorder.
